column1: # MARKER CLASSES -- the family a marker belongs to, and what that family looks
# like by default.
# A row in markers.tsv names its class; the class supplies the default SHAPE and
# COLOUR, and the row overrides either one.
# ⭐ WHY CLASSES EXIST (DL J7, 2026-08-04). Every marker used to be a confidence
# claim, and that narrowness was genuinely the feature: you can ask "what is
# unconfirmed across this whole site" only while every row answers the same
# question. When terminology arrived it was nearly built as a SECOND, parallel
# family -- two mechanisms for one concept -- because the table had no way to say
# which KIND a row was. Michael's ruling: it IS a marker, put it in markers, you
# have found CLASSES. The report groups by class, so the confidence question stays
# answerable no matter how many glossary terms a site marks.
# ADDING A MARKER is a row in markers.tsv. ADDING A WHOLE FAMILY is a row here.
# Neither is a code change and neither is a CSS change -- the class colour is
# emitted as generated CSS by docrender/markers.py.
# COLUMNS
# class    the token a markers.tsv row names
# shape    default shape for the family: box · plain · strike · soft
# color    default colour: any token from EITHER colour table, or a literal
#          hex/oklch
# wash     BOX SHAPES ONLY. How much of the marker's own colour tints the chip
#          behind the text, as a percentage. BLANK inherits the 10% baked into
#          the `.dr-mark--box` fallback, so every existing family renders
#          byte-identically to before this column existed.
# label    what this family MEANS. For the reader of this file and the report.
# ⭐ `wash` EXISTS BECAUSE THE HIGHLIGHT FAMILY NEEDED A FIFTH SHAPE AND DID NOT
# GET ONE (2026-08-07). Michael asked for a highlighter that renders a box like
# `tbc` does. The chip ALREADY had a tinted ground -- `color-mix(... 10%,
# transparent)` -- so nothing was missing; 10% is simply below the threshold
# where a reader registers it as highlighting rather than as a border.
# The obvious move was a `mark` shape with a heavier tint. Rejected: the closed
# set of four is argued in THREE files on the grounds that a reader can tell four
# shapes apart at a glance and cannot tell nine, and "same shape, more tint" is
# not a new shape -- it is the same shape with a different number in it. ⚑ A
# request for a new VARIANT is a request for a new PARAMETER far more often than
# it is a request for a new KIND, and the tell is whether you can state the
# difference without using a number.
# ⚠️ WASH AND COLOUR ARE NOT INDEPENDENT, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS NOT A FREE DIAL.
# The chip text sits on a wash of ITSELF, so raising it lowers the contrast
# between the two. markers.tsv's header already says to measure the chip and not
# the page; that warning now has a knob attached to it, so measure after changing
# this cell rather than after changing only `color`.
# 🔴 `terminology` ASKED FOR `accent-soft` FOR TWO DAYS AND NEVER GOT IT, AND THE
# COMMENT THAT USED TO SIT HERE EXPLAINED IT AS A PLAN. Two things were wrong.
# 1. THE VALIDATOR COULD NOT SEE IT. `_known_tokens()` read only the nine-token
#    stand-in, so every canonical token except `accent` and `warn` was refused --
#    reported unknown once per build and silently painted in the body colour.
#    Fixed 2026-08-05: the two tables are unioned.
# 2. RED AND `accent-soft` WAS THE WRONG TOKEN ANYWAY, which the fallback hid.
#    It is a tinted GROUND, not a text colour: on eos dark it is #1a2b42, a
#    near-black navy measuring 1.4:1 on the canvas. Had the validator accepted
#    it on the day it was written, the terminology marker would have rendered
#    invisible. The fallback to body colour is the only reason nobody noticed.
# ⚑ Worth keeping: A BROKEN REFERENCE THAT DEGRADES GRACEFULLY CAN HIDE A SECOND,
# WORSE MISTAKE UNDERNEATH IT. The report said "unknown token" and everyone read
# that as "not vendored yet" rather than "and also wrong."
# `accent-2` is the Eos TRACKED violet -- 6.63 dark / 5.81 light against the
# canvas -- and it is semantically right as well as legible: on the console it
# is the colour of a named, tracked value, which is exactly what a defined term
# is. ⭐ Still ONE CELL: the token is named here and nowhere else, so changing it
# again is a data edit. The moment a second surface hardcodes it, that is dead.
# ⚠️ `highlight` TAKES `accent` ON MICHAEL'S RULING, AGAINST MY RECOMMENDATION,
# AND HIS REASONING IS THE ONE THAT SURVIVES (2026-08-07). I argued for `accent-2`
# because `accent` already paints the `note` CALLOUT and a highlight is closer to
# the `abstract` register. He pointed out that `accent-2` already paints a MARKER
# -- terminology, one row below -- and that the callout collision costs nothing
# because a box and an inline chip are different surfaces a reader never compares.
# ⭐ THE GENERAL RULE, WRITTEN DOWN BECAUSE IT DECIDES THE NEXT FAMILY TOO:
# COLOUR COLLISIONS ONLY COUNT WITHIN A SURFACE. Two callouts sharing a token is
# the documented design (`tip`/`success`/`good` all take `good`). blocks.tsv can
# reuse freely. ~~Two INLINE MARKERS sharing one would be a genuine defect,
# because they appear in the same sentence, at the same size, and the only thing
# telling them apart is the paint.~~ STRUCK 2026-08-09 -- see the next section,
# which is the amendment and not an exception to this.
# ⭐ AND THE THIRD BOXED FAMILY DID NOT GET TO PICK A COLOUR AT ALL, WHICH IS A
# BETTER ANSWER THAN THE ONE THIS FILE WAS HOLDING (2026-08-09, Michael's ruling).
# The rule above was written when the four boxed markers were amber, green, red
# and blue -- one hue per meaning, and a reader genuinely does separate them by
# paint. `layout` was the fifth, the palette had one distinct hue left, and this
# file's own 🚩 said to measure it against both incumbents first. I measured, and
# then Michael refused the whole frame: *"i don't care if they're visually
# identical. the reporting tag is usually to be different. the front end would
# begin to look like skittles if everything had its own color at this point."*
# ⚑ THE CORRECTED RULE, AND IT IS NARROWER THAN WHAT IT REPLACES: a colour
# collision is a defect only where the COLOUR IS CARRYING THE MEANING. A reader
# separates `conf` from `gap` by paint, so those must stay apart. Nobody reads a
# `.calc` chip and asks how confident it is -- the TAG carries that meaning, the
# report consumes the tag, and the paint is only saying "this is marked." ⭐ The
# tell that the old rule was too wide: it was derived from ONE family type
# (confidence, where hue IS the semantics) and then stated about all of them.
# ⚠️ SO `layout` AND `highlight` BOTH TAKE `accent` AND DIFFER ONLY BY WASH
# (10% against 25%), AND THAT IS DELIBERATE, NOT AN OVERSIGHT. Do not "fix" it.
# The one thing that WOULD be a defect is a reader needing to tell them apart and
# being unable to -- if that ever comes up, the answer is a different SHAPE or a
# different tag, never a fifth hue.
# 🗄️ THE FMP FAMILIES (`layout` + `schema`), 2026-08-09. Owner: FMP Fiona.
# These two exist to document a FileMaker solution in git, and the reason there
# are TWO is not what it looks like. It is not layout-object versus not-an-object
# -- a relationship and a calculation are both objects, and Michael said so when
# the first split was proposed on those grounds. The line that survived:
#   layout   A CONTROL THE USER ACTS ON. A button, a field on a layout. It lives
#            in Layout mode and a reader meets it in prose, mid-sentence.
#   schema   HOW THE DATA IS SHAPED. A calculation, a relationship, a trigger, a
#            global, a value list. It lives in the Graph and in Manage, and a
#            reader meets it inside a table of fields.
# FileMaker's own two halves. The test is what the object IS, and nothing else.
# 🔴 AND THAT TEST IS NARROWER THAN THE ONE THIS SECTION SHIPPED WITH THREE HOURS
# AGO, WHICH WAS WRONG (2026-08-09, corrected before the row that contradicted it
# landed). The original text defined `schema` as *"FileMaker has NO surface that
# enumerates these, so this doc is not a pointer, IT IS THE REGISTER"* -- and
# that is a genuinely load-bearing observation about `calc`, `trigger` and
# `global`. It is simply not what makes something `schema`.
# `.vl` is what caught it. A value list is unmistakably data-shape, and
# **Manage > Value Lists lists every one of them** -- so under the shipped
# definition the correct row would have joined the family while contradicting
# its stated reason for existing.
# ⚑ THE GENERALISABLE PART, AND IT IS WHY THIS IS WORTH THE PARAGRAPH: THE FIRST
# FOUR ROWS PASSED BOTH TESTS, SO ONE SENTENCE WAS WRITTEN FOR TWO PROPOSITIONS
# AND NOTHING COULD TELL THEM APART. "Is it data-shape" and "does FileMaker fail
# to enumerate it" agreed on calc, rel, trigger and global, and a definition
# validated only against cases where two tests agree has not been validated at
# all. The fifth row is the first place they diverge, and a definition is only
# ever tested by the case that splits it. Same shape as the `base` theme
# reaching thirteen callout families with two tokens: correct on everything
# anybody had looked at.
# ✅ SO THE ENUMERATION GAP IS DEMOTED FROM A DEFINITION TO A PER-ROW PROPERTY,
# and it is recorded in each marker's TOOLTIP in markers.tsv, where it varies
# honestly, rather than asserted here about all of them. It is still the reason
# `calc` earns its keep hardest -- nothing in FileMaker lists calculations -- and
# it is now a fact about `calc`, not a claim about the family.
# ⭐ THE RETURN IS THE BUILD REPORT EITHER WAY. Every use is counted and grouped
# by class by markers.py, so `schema` answers "every calculation across this doc
# set" in one block. That was always the point, and it needed a TAG, never a hue.
# ⚠️ TWO FAMILIES RATHER THAN ONE FMP FAMILY, FOR THE SAME REASON CLASSES EXIST
# AT ALL. One family would answer "show me the FileMaker things," which nobody
# needs. Two answer "every relationship" and "every control" separately, and the
# report is only worth reading while each class answers ONE question.
# ⚠️ `schema` IS `plain` ON PURPOSE. These are typed inside data-table cells
# (`[Text]{.calc}` in a .tsv), and a boxed chip in every cell of a table is a
# wall. `layout` is boxed because it appears in prose, where a control being
# named wants to look like a control. Same reasoning as `terminology`, which is
# also plain and also lives mid-sentence.
# 🚩 NOT BUILT, NAMED SO IT IS NOT RE-DISCOVERED: `portal`, `tab` and `popover`
# were raised as `layout` candidates and DEFERRED by Michael on 2026-08-09. They
# are real, they are just not yet typed anywhere. The build report is what should
# decide them -- add the family when the marker is being reached for, not before.
